claim: Secondary growth of Arabidopsis hypocotyls creates a radial pattern of highly specialized tissues that comprises several thousand cells starting from a few dozen.
source: Secondary growth of Arabidopsis hypocotyls creates a radial pattern of highly specialized tissues that comprises several thousand cells starting from a few dozen.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a description of the biological process being studied.

claim: The automated quantitative histology approach established a cellular resolution atlas that reveals vascular morphodynamics during secondary growth.
source: Coupled with automated cell type recognition through machine learning, we could establish a cellular resolution atlas that reveals vascular morphodynamics during secondary growth, for example equidistant phloem pole formation.
evidence: This is the main finding stated in the abstract, supported by the methods and results described throughout the manuscript.

claim: Equidistant phloem pole formation occurs during secondary growth.
source: we could establish a cellular resolution atlas that reveals vascular morphodynamics during secondary growth, for example equidistant phloem pole formation.
evidence: This is stated as an example finding in the abstract and supported by data in Figure 6.

claim: Arabidopsis thaliana is a small, annual dicotyledon of the Brassicaceae family.
source: Arabidopsis thaliana (Arabidopsis), a small, annual dicotyledon of the Brassicaceae family, is the model of choice for developmental biology of higher plants
evidence: This is a direct statement about the taxonomic classification of Arabidopsis.

claim: The meristematic and differentiation regions of the Arabidopsis root tip comprise a mere 5–6 dozen cells in the radial dimension.
source: the meristematic and differentiation regions of the root tip comprise a mere 5–6 dozen cells in the radial dimension and can be imaged all across using state-of-the-art microscopes
evidence: This is stated directly in the text with a citation to Dolan et al., 1993.

claim: The vascular cambium produces xylem tissues towards the inside and phloem tissues towards the outside.
source: The latter are produced by another cylindrical secondary meristem, the vascular cambium, which produces xylem tissues towards the inside and phloem tissues towards the outside
evidence: This is stated directly with citations to Nieminen et al., 2004 and Groover and Robischon, 2006.

claim: Formation of xylem tissues through secondary growth is the main process of durable biomass accumulation in plants.
source: Formation of xylem tissues through secondary growth is the main process of durable biomass accumulation in plants and most prominent in tree trunks
evidence: This is stated directly in the introduction.

claim: Two principal phases of hypocotyl secondary growth exist: an early phase of proportional growth and a later phase of xylem expansion.
source: Previous work has identified two principal phases of hypocotyl secondary growth, an early phase of proportional growth, when the cambium produces phloem and xylem tissues at roughly equal rates, and a later phase of xylem expansion, when the relative production of xylem dominates the radial expansion
evidence: This is stated with citations to Chaffey et al., 2002 and Sibout et al., 2008.

claim: Early phase xylem consists mainly of interconnected xylem vessels and xylem parenchyma cells.
source: Early phase xylem consists mainly of the interconnected xylem vessels (terminally differentiated, dead cells with perforated, thick cell walls that are the actual conducts for water and solutes) and xylem parenchyma cells.
evidence: This is a direct description of tissue composition.

claim: Early phase phloem comprises sieve elements, companion cells, and phloem parenchyma cells.
source: Early phase phloem comprises the sieve elements (interconnected, enucleated but alive cells that perform the actual transport of the phloem sap), companion cells (which provide basic metabolism for sieve elements and are responsible for loading and un-loading of phloem sap cargo) and phloem parenchyma cells.
evidence: This is a direct description of tissue composition.

claim: The transition between early phase and xylem expansion phase is triggered by the onset of flowering.
source: It has been shown that the transition between the early phase and the xylem expansion phase is triggered by the onset of flowering
evidence: This is stated with a citation to Sibout et al., 2008.

claim: The transition between early phase and xylem expansion phase is triggered by gibberellin, a mobile shoot-derived signal.
source: It has been shown that the transition between the early phase and the xylem expansion phase is triggered by the onset of flowering (Sibout et al., 2008), through a mobile shoot-derived signal, the plant hormone gibberellin
evidence: This is stated with a citation to Ragni et al., 2011.

claim: Col-0 and Ler display divergent secondary growth dynamics.
source: For analysis we chose two common laboratory accessions, Columbia-0 (Col-0) and Landsberg erecta (Ler), which have already been shown to display divergent secondary growth dynamics
evidence: This is stated with a citation to Ragni et al., 2011.

claim: Five time points were analyzed in detail, starting at 15 days after germination (dag) and ending at 35 dag.
source: we chose to analyze five time points in detail, starting at 15 days after germination (dag), when a full cambium is established and the initial outer epidermal and cortex cell layers are already or about to be shed. This was followed by additional sampling at 20, 25, 30 and up to 35 dag
evidence: This is a direct statement about the experimental design.

claim: All plants of both genotypes flowered at 17 dag ±1 d under the experimental conditions.
source: In our conditions, all plants of both genotypes flowered at 17 dag ±1 d.
evidence: This is a direct observation from the experiments.

claim: The average hypocotyl stele diameter was ca. 0.3 mm in Col-0 and ca. 0.15 mm in Ler at 15 dag.
source: Whereas the average hypocotyl stele diameter was ca. 0.3 mm in Col-0 and ca. 0.15 mm in Ler at 15 dag
evidence: This is a direct measurement reported in the results.

claim: The radial expansion resulted in an average diameter of 1.6 mm in Col-0 and 1.1 mm in Ler at 35 dag.
source: the radial expansion resulted in an average diameter of 1.6 mm in Col-0 and 1.1 mm in Ler at 35 dag.
evidence: This is a direct measurement reported in the results.

claim: Relative xylem area increased from 12% to 29% in Col-0 between 15 dag and 35 dag.
source: Concomitantly, relative xylem area increased from 12% to 29% in Col-0
evidence: This is a direct measurement reported in the results.

claim: Relative xylem area increased from 31% to 47% in Ler between 15 dag and 35 dag.
source: and from 31% to 47% in Ler
evidence: This is a direct measurement reported in the results.

claim: The segmentation pipeline performed at more than 99% accuracy (i.e., less than 1% of mis-segmented cells).
source: The pipeline is fully automated and robust and typically performed at more than 99% accuracy (i.e., less than 1% of mis-segmented cells) across the scale of images
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 1F showing the relationship between mis-segmented cells and total cell number.

claim: Overall median cell number at 15 dag was 883 for Col-0 and 260 for Ler.
source: Overall median cell number at 15 dag was 883 for Col-0 and 260 for Ler.
evidence: This is a direct measurement from the segmentation analysis.

claim: At 35 dag, median cell number had increased to 18'124 and 11'026 for Col-0 and Ler, respectively.
source: At 35 dag, it had increased to 18'124 and 11'026, respectively
evidence: This is a direct measurement from the segmentation analysis.

claim: Col-0 showed higher overall secondary growth but Ler showed higher relative secondary growth (ca. 42-fold vs ca. 21-fold increase in cell number).
source: indicating higher overall secondary growth in Col-0, but higher relative secondary growth in Ler (i.e., a ca. 42-fold vs a ca. 21-fold increase in cell number).
evidence: This is calculated from the cell number data.

claim: 16 cellular descriptors representing geometric characteristics of cell shape and relative cell position were computed.
source: we advanced towards our goal of a full cellular resolution analysis by computing 16 cellular descriptors that represent the geometric characteristics of cell shape and relative cell position
evidence: This is stated in the text and detailed in Supplementary file 1A.

claim: The training set for machine learning comprised 3'144 manually labeled cells.
source: The training set was a subset of our data that comprised a total of 3'144 manually labeled cells, dispatched into two sections per time point and genotype
evidence: This is a direct statement about the training data.

claim: Five distinct cell type categories could be classified and quantified across all sections and time points.
source: Across all sections and time points, a common set of five distinct cell type categories (Supplementary file 1D) could be classified and quantified, that is (i) xylem vessels and parenchymatic cells, (ii) xylem fibers, (iii) cambial cells, (iv) phloem bundle cells (companion cells and sieve elements) and (v) parenchymatic phloem cells (including any of the rare phloem fibers)
evidence: This is stated directly in the results section.

claim: The morphology- and position-based approach identified cells with an average accuracy of 88% and a median accuracy of 95%.
source: For these categories, our purely morphology- and position-based approach identified cells with an average accuracy of 88% and a median accuracy of 95% across the n = 50 cell type category X time point X genotype matrix.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the classification performance.

claim: Xylem area expansion rate was nearly equal in both Col-0 and Ler genotypes.
source: However, xylem area expansion rate was nearly equal in both genotypes
evidence: This is stated in the text and can be observed in Figure 3C.

claim: The number of xylem cells and the xylem cell proliferation rate were close in both Col-0 and Ler genotypes.
source: Quantification of cell proliferation confirmed that the number of xylem cells and the xylem cell proliferation rate were close in both genotypes
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 3D.

claim: The total number of cells in Ler was ca. twofold lower than in Col-0.
source: however the total number of cells in Ler was ca. twofold lower than in Col-0
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 3E.

claim: The phloem proliferation rate was more than twofold lower in Ler compared to Col-0.
source: Moreover, the phloem proliferation rate was more than twofold lower in Ler
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 3D.

claim: Phloem cell number stagnated between 30 and 35 dag in Ler.
source: with stagnation in phloem cell number between 30 and 35 dag
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 3D.

claim: A plateau in cambial growth combined with stagnating phloem proliferation is responsible for overall reduced radial growth but relatively increased xylem expansion in Ler.
source: In summary, our results suggest that a plateau in cambial growth combined with stagnating phloem proliferation is responsible for overall reduced radial growth but relatively increased xylem expansion in Ler.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the data presented in Figure 3.

claim: No distinguishable vascular organization of cell orientation was yet built up at 15 dag in Col-0.
source: the incline angle was uniformly distributed at 15 dag in Col-0 (Hartigans' dip test p>10−3), meaning that no distinguishable vascular organization of cell orientation was yet built up.
evidence: This is stated in the text based on statistical analysis and supported by Figure 4C.

claim: A discernable bimodal distribution of incline angles emerged at 30 dag in Col-0.
source: At 30 dag, a second peak towards higher values of incline arose, giving shape to a discernable bimodal distribution (Hartigans' dip test p<2.2 × 10−6)
evidence: This is stated in the text based on statistical analysis and supported by Figure 4C.

claim: Sharp bimodal-shaped density curves at later time points in Ler supported the coexistence of two populations of cells, a mostly radially and a mostly orthoradially oriented one.
source: At the later time points, sharp bimodal-shaped density curves supported the coexistence of two populations of cells, a mostly radially and a mostly orthoradially oriented one (Hartigans' dip test p<2.2 × 10−6), similar to Col-0.
evidence: This is stated in the text based on statistical analysis and supported by Figure 4D.

claim: Practically no post-cambial divisions were observed in the xylem area.
source: In the xylem area, practically no post-cambial divisions were observed (Figure 5—figure supplement 1)
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Radial cell files in xylem were generally continuous with the adjacent cambial files.
source: and radial cell files were generally continuous with the adjacent cambial files.
evidence: This is based on visual inspection of cross sections as stated in the text.

claim: Cellular growth in xylem resulted in a switch from orthoradial to radial orientation.
source: Following such cell files also suggested that cellular growth led to a switch in xylem cell incline angle orientation. Whereas xylem cells that emerged from the cambium still retained the orthoradial orientation, cellular growth eventually resulted in a switch towards a radial orientation.
evidence: This is based on visual inspection and analysis of cell files.

claim: Practically no cell divisions, neither anticlinal nor periclinal, were observed in phloem parenchyma cells.
source: Similar to the xylem however, phloem cells were typically in continuity with the corresponding cambial cell files, and practically no cell divisions, neither anticlinal nor periclinal, were observed.
evidence: This is based on visual inspection of cross sections.

claim: Numerous post-cambial divisions, both anticlinal and periclinal, were observed in cell files that ended up in vascular bundles.
source: The exceptions to this were cell files that ended up in vascular bundles. In these, numerous post-cambial divisions could be observed, both in the anticlinal and periclinal orientations.
evidence: This is based on visual inspection of cross sections.

claim: The vast majority of cell divisions was observed in the cambium.
source: Finally, as expected the vast majority of cell divisions was observed in the cambium.
evidence: This is based on visual inspection of cross sections.

claim: The radial expansion of hypocotyls is mostly driven by cambial activity and very little by post-cambial cell divisions.
source: In summary, the radial expansion of hypocotyls appeared to be mostly driven by cambial activity and very little by post-cambial cell divisions.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the observations of cell division patterns.

claim: Phloem pole formation displays a precise periodicity with a constant arc distance of ca. 62 pixels between phloem poles.
source: The dominant single peak indicates a constant arc distance of ca. 62 pixel between the phloem poles.
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 6C.

claim: A constant arc interspace distance for phloem pole formation was found along the developmental time series with a concomitant decrease in the interspace angle due to overall secondary growth.
source: we found a constant arc interspace distance for phloem pole formation along the developmental time series with a concomitant decrease in the interspace angle due to the overall secondary growth.
evidence: This is stated as a finding in the discussion section.

claim: A reaction-diffusion model with a growing boundary would be consistent with the phloem pole patterning results.
source: A reaction-diffusion model with a growing boundary (i.e., representing the expanding xylem area) would be consistent with these results.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the data.

claim: The growing xylem area might exert a compression force on surrounding cambial and parenchymal cells, forcing them into tangential anisotropic cell elongation.
source: One possible explanation for this phenomenon could be tissue mechanics. The growing xylem area might exert a compression force on surrounding cambial and parenchymal cells, forcing them into tangential anisotropic cell elongation.
evidence: This is presented as a possible explanation for observed phenomena.

claim: A receptor-like kinase—peptide ligand pair is involved in cambial polarity and interacts with hormone signaling pathways.
source: For instance, polarity of the cambium to produce xylem to the inside and phloem to the outside is an inherent feature of secondary growth. A receptor-like kinase—peptide ligand pair is involved in this process and interacts with hormone signaling pathways
evidence: This is stated with citations to Hirakawa et al., 2008, 2010 and Etchells et al., 2012.

claim: The phenotypic penetrance of cambial polarity mutants is background-dependent, with stronger effects in Ler than in Col-0.
source: Notably, the phenotypic penetrance of the respective mutants is background-dependent, with stronger effects in Ler than in Col-0
evidence: This is stated with a citation to Etchells et al., 2013.

claim: Phloem production in Ler ceases before xylem production.
source: Rather it appears that phloem production in Ler ceases before xylem production and contributes to the divergent growth dynamics in the two genotypes.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the data analysis.

claim: The severely reduced overall cell production in Ler as compared to Col-0 can be mainly attributed to reduced phloem and cambium cell number.
source: The severely reduced overall cell production in Ler as compared to Col-0 can be mainly attributed to reduced phloem and cambium cell number
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the quantitative data.

claim: Initial secondary growth appears to be particularly slow in Ler as indicated by more than threefold difference in cell number at 15 dag.
source: Interestingly, the nearly 50% reduction in overall cell number does not mean that growth is uniformly slower in Ler. Rather, initial secondary growth appears to be particularly slow in Ler as indicated by more than threefold difference in cell number at 15 dag.
evidence: This is based on comparison of cell number data between genotypes.

claim: Cell production in Ler accelerates between 15 dag and 25 dag, surpassing Col-0 in relative terms.
source: This is followed by an acceleration of cell production that surpasses Col-0 in relative terms between 15 dag and 25 dag
evidence: This is based on analysis of cell proliferation rates over time.

claim: Both Col-0 and Ler reach overall similar end points in secondary growth as revealed by principal component analysis.
source: This pattern is also evident from the principal component analysis, in which both Col-0 and Ler reach overall similar end points.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 3A.

claim: The analysis along a series of time points revealed highly divergent secondary growth dynamics in the genotypes that would not have been evident from a comparison of end points.
source: Thus, our analysis along a series of time points has revealed highly divergent secondary growth dynamics in the genotypes that would not have been evident from a comparison of end points.
evidence: This is a conclusion about the value of the time-series approach.

claim: The watershed algorithm with automatic seeding was used to identify cell boundaries.
source: A variant watershed algorithm with automatic seeding (http://bigwww.epfl.ch/sage/soft/watershed) was used to identify the cell boundaries.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the methods used.

claim: Support vector machine (SVM) with C-classification and radial basis function (RBF) kernel was used for cell type classification.
source: One classifier was built per genotype and per time point (Supplementary file 1C) using the C-classification with a radial basis function (RBF) kernel of the support vector machine
evidence: This is a direct statement about the machine learning method used.

claim: Plants were grown in soil in a 16 hr light–8 hr dark cycle at 22°C with 150 µE light intensity.
source: Plants were grown in soil in a 16 hr light–8 hr dark cycle at 22°C with 150 µE light intensity.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the growth conditions.

claim: Embedding was performed using plastic resin, which proved to be the only robust method to acquire 3 µm thin cross-sections while conserving the cellular structure.
source: Embedding was performed using plastic resin, which proved to be the only robust method to acquire 3 µm thin cross-sections while conserving the cellular structure.
evidence: This is a statement about the methodological approach and its justification.

claim: Individual cross section images were assembled from a minimum of 9 (3 × 3) up to 144 (12 × 12) panels.
source: Individual cross section images subjected to segmentation were thus assembled from a minimum of 9 (3 × 3) up to 144 (12 × 12) panels
evidence: This is stated in the text and illustrated in Figure 1C.

claim: CPU time scaled exponentially with image size, taking ca. 8 min. for a 15 dag sample but ca. 1000 min for a 35 dag sample.
source: However, because CPU time scaled exponentially with image size, taking ca. 8 min. for a 15 dag sample but ca. 1000 min for a 35 dag sample, computation eventually became limiting for our endeavor.
evidence: This is a direct statement about computational performance.

claim: The analysis was restricted to ca. 20 selected cross sections per genotype and time point (i.e., 208 cross sections in total, requiring ca. 800 hr of total CPU time).
source: Thus, we restricted our analysis to ca. 20 selected cross sections per genotype and time point (i.e., 208 cross sections in total, requiring ca. 800 hr of total CPU time)
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The patterning of phloem pole position is already laid down in the cambium.
source: Since there appeared to be no cessation of cell division in the cell files connecting the cambium and the vascular bundles, the data suggested that the patterning of phloem pole position might already be laid down in the cambium.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation of continuous cell division in files connecting cambium to vascular bundles.

claim: The best combination of descriptors for cell type classification varied with the time point and genotype analyzed.
source: Feature selection is a well-known pivotal issue in machine learning, and indeed the best combination of descriptors was critical in automated cell type classification and varied with the time point and genotype analyzed
evidence: This is stated as an observation about the machine learning approach.

claim: Cell type-specific position can vary with the age of the section.
source: mainly because cell type-specific position can vary with the age of the section.
evidence: This is stated as an explanation for why feature selection varied.

claim: Xylem vessels and phloem parenchyma cells increasingly resemble each other in their outlines as secondary growth proceeds.
source: This was particularly prevalent at the later stages of development and could be pinpointed to a frequent confusion between xylem vessels and phloem parenchyma cells, which increasingly resemble each other in their outlines as secondary growth proceeds.
evidence: This is stated as an explanation for classification difficulties.

claim: The uniformity in plant cell shape hampered the identification of certain cell states by the machine learning approach.
source: To some degree, this uniformity in cell shape hampered the identification of certain cell states by our machine learning approach, for instance the direct identification of dividing cells.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of the approach.

claim: Adding tissue-related features such as cell connectivity and cell wall thickness might overcome obstacles in cell type classification and greatly increase performance.
source: Adding tissue-related features, such as cell connectivity (i.e., the number of neighboring cells), and improving the segmentation algorithm such that cell wall thickness could be incorporated into the analyses might overcome these obstacles and greatly increase performance.
evidence: This is presented as a suggestion for future improvement.

claim: The approach should be universally applicable for any tissue or organ from which cell outlines can be segmented after imaging and for which a reference point can be defined.
source: The latter should be possible for any tissue or organ from which cell outlines can be segmented after imaging and for which a reference point can be defined, for example (partial) sections from tree trunks or confocal images of root meristems.
evidence: This is stated as a claim about the generalizability of the method.

claim: The growing xylem area might exert a compression force that is perceived and conveyed into cellular behavior through katanins and dynamic reorientation of microtubules.
source: How such mechanical stress is perceived and conveyed into cellular behavior is largely enigmatic and an emerging hot topic in plant biology, where first studies on shoot apical meristem formation have implicated katanins in the dynamic reorientation of microtubules perpendicular to stress direction
evidence: This is inferred from cited work on mechanical stress perception with a citation to Uyttewaal et al., 2012.

claim: A gradual increase and arrangement of cambial cells together with orthoradial cellular organization of surrounding tissues appeared to be a prerequisite for proper xylem development and relative xylem expansion around 20–25 dag.
source: Our data indicate a gradual increase and arrangement of cambial cells, which together with orthoradial cellular organization of the surrounding tissues appeared to be a prerequisite for proper xylem development and relative xylem expansion around 20–25 dag.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the spatio-temporal analysis of cell incline angles.

claim: The spatio-temporal dynamics of overall incline captured the distinct phases of secondary growth progression.
source: Interestingly, the spatio-temporal dynamics of the overall incline (i.e., covering the whole section cell content at a given time point) captured the distinct phases of secondary growth progression described above.
evidence: This is stated as an observation about the incline angle analysis.

claim: Mostly radial orientation could be an indicator for the prevalence of anticlinal division planes, whereas mostly orthoradial orientations could be an indicator for the prevalence of periclinal ones.
source: The distribution of inclines also had possible implications for the orientation of cell divisions, in the sense that mostly radial orientation could be an indicator for the prevalence of anticlinal division planes, whereas mostly orthoradial orientations could be an indicator for the prevalence of periclinal ones.
evidence: This is presented as a possible interpretation of the incline data.

claim: Visual inspection of cross sections suggested that incline orientation is not a direct indicator of division plane orientation.
source: Visual inspection of cross sections suggested that this is not the case however
evidence: This is stated based on visual inspection of sections.

claim: A remarkable rarity of post-cambial cell divisions was observed through visual inspection.
source: Visual inspection of cross sections suggested that this is not the case however, also revealing a remarkable rarity of post-cambial cell divisions.
evidence: This is stated based on visual inspection of sections.

claim: Cellular growth in xylem led to a switch in cell incline angle orientation from orthoradial to radial.
source: Following such cell files also suggested that cellular growth led to a switch in xylem cell incline angle orientation.
evidence: This is inferred from following cell files in cross sections.

claim: Such switching in incline angle orientation was not observed in the phloem.
source: Such switching was not observed in the phloem, consistent with the prevalence of orthoradial inclines.
evidence: This is stated based on observations of phloem cells.

claim: Most cambial cell divisions occurred in a perfect periclinal orientation.
source: Mostly, they occurred in a perfect periclinal orientation
evidence: This is stated based on visual inspection of cambial divisions.

claim: Numerous interspersed anticlinal divisions in the cambium are necessary to keep up with overall radial expansion.
source: but we also observed numerous interspersed anticlinal divisions that are necessary to keep up with overall radial expansion.
evidence: This is stated based on observations and functional interpretation.

claim: Local production of mobile ligand and activation of its receptor at a distance are potential candidates for a reaction-diffusion mechanism of phloem pole patterning.
source: Local production of the above-mentioned mobile ligand and activation of its receptor at a distance are potential candidates for such a mechanism.
evidence: This is presented as a speculative mechanism.

claim: Patterning cues from apical sources might direct phloem pole formation, for instance to coordinate it with phyllotaxy.
source: Alternatively, patterning cues from apical sources might direct phloem pole formation, for instance to coordinate it with phyllotaxy.
evidence: This is presented as an alternative speculative mechanism.

claim: Application of quantitative histology approach to complementary stem sections could present one way to explore phloem patterning mechanisms.
source: Application of our quantitative histology approach to complementary stem sections could present one way to explore these possibilities.
evidence: This is presented as a suggestion for future research.

claim: Secondary growth is a major developmental process in dicotyledons, including herbaceous plants such as Arabidopsis.
source: Secondary growth is a major developmental process in dicotyledons, including herbaceaous plants such as Arabidopsis
evidence: This is stated with citations to Chaffey et al., 2002; Sibout et al., 2008; Elo et al., 2009.

claim: Secondary growth is comparatively an under-researched trait.
source: however, it is comparatively an under-researched trait.
evidence: This is stated as an assessment of the field.

claim: A comprehensive description of secondary growth dynamics at the cellular level is still missing.
source: in part to the relatively big scale of the process. Both complications also contribute to the fact that a comprehensive description of secondary growth dynamics at the cellular level is still missing.
evidence: This is stated as a gap in knowledge that the study addresses.

claim: The Arabidopsis hypocotyl poses various advantages as a secondary growth system as opposed to Arabidopsis stems, most notably the uncoupling of elongation growth and secondary growth.
source: As a secondary growth system, we chose the Arabidopsis hypocotyl, which has been shown previously to pose various advantages as opposed to Arabidopsis stems, most notably the uncoupling of elongation growth and secondary growth
evidence: This is stated with a citation to Sibout et al., 2008.

claim: A high-throughput approach was necessary to obtain statistically solid data for secondary growth analysis.
source: While a high-throughput approach was necessary to obtain statistically solid data, high-resolution imaging was required for reliable cellular level analyses.
evidence: This is stated as a justification for the methodological approach.

claim: High-resolution imaging was required for reliable cellular level analyses of secondary growth.
source: While a high-throughput approach was necessary to obtain statistically solid data, high-resolution imaging was required for reliable cellular level analyses.
evidence: This is stated as a justification for the methodological approach.

claim: Quantitative histology combined with machine learning was the only realistic option to achieve both high-throughput and high-resolution analysis.
source: A novel type of global approach, that is, quantitative histology combined with machine learning, was the only realistic option to achieve both goals.
evidence: This is stated as a justification for the methodological approach.

claim: The Support Vector Machine (SVM) method has proven its efficiency in a broad range of life science applications.
source: To this end, we used the Support Vector Machine (SVM) method, because it had already proven its efficiency in a broad range of life science applications
evidence: This is stated with a citation to Noble, 2006.

claim: Plant cells are encapsulated by rigid cell walls that resist the internal turgor pressure.
source: The factors that limited our approach were to some degree related to the properties of plant cells, notably that they are encapsulated by rigid cell walls that resist the internal turgor pressure.
evidence: This is stated as a general property of plant cells.

claim: Cellular geometry in plants is shaped by the material properties of the walls and by the permanent force of turgor pressure.
source: Their cellular geometry is therefore not only shaped by the material properties of the walls, but also by the permanent force of turgor pressure
evidence: This is stated as an explanation for plant cell shape characteristics.

claim: There is reduced variation of cell shape in plants as compared to animals.
source: manifesting in the reduced variation of cell shape in plants as compared to animals
evidence: This is stated with a citation to Theriault et al., 2012.

claim: Binarization of images using an adaptive Gaussian filter greatly accelerated the segmentation procedure.
source: In part, this could be off set by binarization of the images using an adaptive Gaussian filter, which greatly accelerated the segmentation procedure.
evidence: This is stated as a methodological improvement.

claim: Morphological operations on binarized images kept segmentation accuracy high while automating the task.
source: We could compensate an associated decrease in segmentation quality (because watershed segmentation is more accurate on gray scale images) by effectuating morphological operations on the binarized images, thereby keeping segmentation accuracy high while automating the task.
evidence: This is stated as a methodological solution.
